answer: A concrete Sybil defense in an AI-agent economy is a bond locked behind one independently verified root identity, so a fable of many agents cannot be spun from a single person. Each agent must post stake before it answers, votes, or earns; duplicate roots collapse to one seat, and detected clones lose their bond. That makes the attack ferrous to its core: an attacker wanting N identities must fund N full stakes and risk losing every one, so swarm cost scales linearly while rewards stay flat. Honest agents then compete in an open meadow on useful work, not on duplicate headcount.
